title: Merge Intervals
followUps: What is the time complexity, and which step dominates it?
How would you handle intervals arriving one at a time as a stream, where you must keep the merged set up to date?
How would you insert a single new interval into an already-merged, sorted list more efficiently than re-merging everything?
Do touching intervals like [1,4] and [4,5] merge in your solution? Where in the code is that decided, and how would you make it configurable?

interviewer.approach: Sort by start, then sweep: if the current interval's start <= last merged end, extend last end = max(last end, current end); otherwise append. O(n log n) time, O(n) output space.
hints: Would it help if the intervals were in some particular order?
After sorting by start, an interval can only overlap with the one you most recently merged. What do you compare?
When merging, remember the merged end is the max of both ends — one interval can fully contain the next.
pitfalls: Setting end = current end instead of max(end, current end) (fails on containment like [1,10],[2,3]).
Not sorting, or sorting by end instead of start.
Mutating the input in a way that affects the result.
